question.problem:
The students in a particular school are split among three classes, class $1,$ class $2,$ and class $3.$

- Class $1$ contains $25%$ of the students in the school, and $55%$ of those students take biology.

- Class $2$ contains $35%$ of the students in the school, and $40%$ of those students take biology.

- Class $3$ contains $40%$ of the students in the school.

If $45%$ of students in the entire school are female, $80%$ of female students take biology, and $70%$ of biology students are female, what is the probability that a randomly selected student from class $3$ takes biology? Round your answer to $3$ decimal places.
question.worked_solution:
Let $F$ be the event that a student is female, $B$ be the event that a student takes biology, and ${C}_{1},{C}_{2},{C}_{3}$ be the event that a student is in class $1,$ $2,$ or $3,$ respectively. 

Let's break down the information given in the problem statement:

- From the bullet points, we have the following information:

$$
\begin{aligned} & P({C}_{1})=0.25 &  & P(B|{C}_{1})=0.55 \\  & P({C}_{2})=0.35 &  & P(B|{C}_{2})=0.4 \\  & P({C}_{3})=0.4\end{aligned}
$$

The disjoint union ${C}_{1}⊔{C}_{2}⊔{C}_{3}$ covers the entire sample space, and we have

$$
P({C}_{1})+P({C}_{2})+P({C}_{3})=0.25+0.35+0.4=1.
$$

- Since $45%$ of students in the entire school are female, we have

$$
P(F)=0.45.
$$

- Since $80%$ of females take biology, we have

$$
P(B|F)=0.8.
$$

- Since $70%$ of biology students are female, we have

$$
P(F|B)=0.7.
$$

We want to find the probability that a randomly chosen student from class $3$ takes biology, which is represented as $P(B|{C}_{3}).$ 

Using Bayes' theorem combined with the law of total probability, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(F|B) & =\frac{P(B|F)P(F)}{P(B)} \\ P(F|B) & =\frac{P(B|F)P(F)}{P(B|{C}_{1})P({C}_{1})+P(B|{C}_{2})P({C}_{2})+P(B|{C}_{3})P({C}_{3})} \\ 0.7 & =\frac{(0.8)(0.45)}{(0.55)(0.25)+(0.4)(0.35)+P(B|{C}_{3})(0.4)} \\ 0.7 & =\frac{0.36}{0.2775+0.4P(B|{C}_{3})}.\end{aligned}
$$

Solving this equation for $P(B|{C}_{3}),$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}0.7(0.2775+0.4P(B|{C}_{3})) & =0.36 \\ 0.2775+0.4P(B|{C}_{3}) & =\frac{0.36}{0.7} \\ 0.2775+0.4P(B|{C}_{3}) & =\frac{18}{35} \\ 0.4P(B|{C}_{3}) & =\frac{18}{35}-0.2775 \\ P(B|{C}_{3}) & =\frac{1}{0.4}(\frac{18}{35}-0.2775) \\ P(B|{C}_{3}) & ≈0.592\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to three decimal places.
